description: Checklist §4.2 (C4.10): each configuration row and what carries it. `dimension`: rows of core/policy/policy-dimensions.json, resolved, narrowed and lockable by the one resolver (QA-2 and C4.02's vectors hold every row); `flag`: operator env in flags.json, set by the deployment alone; `section`: a policy-layer section a feature reads directly; `partial` and `missing` name what is left and the package that adds it. tests/cohesion/test_c4_10_config_surface.py holds this file to the checklist, the dimension table and flags.json.

rows.note: engines are admitted by kind or kind@version selectors, narrowed per layer; the release allowlist names the versions a deployment can run (one per engine ships today, which is a release fact, not a setting)
unpinned, a run takes its engine's first admitted allowlist entry, the latest approved; an org or agent selector `kind@version` pins one; a conversation keeps the version it started on (C14.01)
the backend is the deployment's; the weakest runtime a run accepts narrows per layer

each lowers the engine template's value, never raises it (default: the template's); the workspace's disk quota is operator env; the largest input is the deployment's HARNESS_INPUT_MAX_MB (100 MiB), which sandbox.inputMaxMb lowers for an org (J-26)
operator env: the broker's pool is per host, not per template, so no layer below the deployment sets it
a run's lifetime narrows per layer. An engine sandbox is released at the end of every turn (keep-warm 0), so a run has no idle sandbox to time out; a signed-in sandbox's idle time is operator env
7 days in the release; the deployment or the org may shorten it. The retention sweeper deletes older snapshots and admission never carries one

an engine asks for one neutral model id, which the model gateway maps to the run's pinned primary route (MG-06, C3.61); `pipeshub:org-default` names the org's default model; named roles map to an org's models per layer; a vendor name is refused, never mapped. Default: the org's default model

the setup phase is the run's agent-phase egress plus its repository, fetch-only, with the person's read token (WP-26), then dropped; a clone a person approves is fetched by the worker outside the sandbox from the `repositories` hosts (WP-63)

run images carry their packages and no installer; a registry or an internal mirror is a site an admin allows (the `package-registries` preset, or the mirror's host) under `websites`, off by default; a deployment's corporate proxy is EGRESS_UPSTREAM_PROXY

the hosts an agent may ask to clone from, per org and narrowed per agent, off by default. Push policy is fixed, not a setting: only the session branch, fast-forward, each push approved by a person (GT-02/03, OWD); git hosts are never reachable from a sandbox
which items an agent holds are control-plane grants (CPD-7), not a dimension
operator tuning; an agent that wants every tool listed picks toolDisclosure.mode eager

null: each executor's own (the loop 64,000 characters, an engine 24,000, about 8k tokens); a set value lowers both. Past it an engine's knowledge results go to /pipeshub/knowledge and other results are cut head and tail with how to get the rest
the org's allowed formats and the agent's default; unset: concise. A model may still ask for either format in a call
the flow rule is a member of the approval rules (approvals.flow)

how long a run waits for an answer, narrowed per layer (default: the deployment's 7 days, not the 1 hour proposed: a person away for a meeting should not lose the run); the person the run acts for approves
on by default; off, every call is asked. Plan approvals and an edition's asks are never answered for the conversation

rows.setting: Budgets: tokens / cost / turns / wall-clock / sandbox-seconds
rows.note: per run: the dimensions narrow per layer (the USD cap is the real limit, tokens a backstop)

runs queued or running at once: 200 per org and 10 per person in the release (not the 10 / 2 proposed, which would refuse a team's ordinary use), lowered by the deployment or the org; sandbox caps are operator env
on by default where the model exposes reasoning; off, reasoning is never sent to the browser
read-only by default (true); hidden (false) sends commands by name only, never their output

a layer section the retention sweeper reads (E7); default: no expiry, configurable per org, not the 90 days / 1 year the table proposed. Audit records hold ids and counts only and stay with the org (CLEANUP-G1)

Labs turns scheduled runs on per org; a webhook trigger's body cap and per-minute rate are ceilings the deployment or the org may lower. Catch-up, overlap and the webhook's signature are each schedule's own (TR-02, TR-04, TR-06)
the org's ceiling of channels (in_app, email, slack), in-app by default; each schedule's owner picks among them for its completion notice (TR-07), and approver link notices use the same ceiling.
operator env: the exporter is per process
on by default: a run whose worker was lost is queued again and resumes from its checkpoint; a call whose outcome is unknown is reconciled or asked, never repeated. Off: the run ends as interrupted
dev/test only: the release's gVisor floor is the one override
